principles.title: Scopes of the app
principles.text: An app with only `content:read` cannot call a write action, even if the user can.

principles.title: Permissions of the user
principles.text: Actions run as the backend user. Page permissions, table and field access and workspaces apply as usual.

calculator.title: Scope calculator
calculator.intro: The scopes of an OAuth token are the intersection of the scopes that the app requests, the scopes that an administrator configured for the app and the scopes that the user can hold. Change the values and select a user.
calculator.note: In an action that the token can call, the permissions of the user still apply. On every request, EXT:hub intersects the scopes of the token with the current configuration of the app again, so when an administrator removes a scope from an app, the change applies immediately.

mcp.denied: Without the scope `mcp`, the core rejects the request to `/typo3/api/mcp` with `403 Missing scope: mcp`. The token can call no MCP tool.

mcp.title: Scopes in MCP tool calls
mcp.intro: The MCP server is the action `mcp`. The core checks the scopes of the HTTP request once, for the action `mcp`. Every MCP tool inside then runs with the same backend user and the same scopes, and the MCP server lists and calls only the MCP tools whose scopes the token grants.

steps.title: Scopes of the request
steps.text: EXT:hub validates the token and sets the scopes of the HTTP request. For an OAuth app, the scopes are the scopes of the token that the configuration of the app still contains. For a static app, the scopes are the scopes of the app.

steps.title: Scope mcp
steps.text: The request handler checks the scopes of the action `mcp`. Without the scope `mcp`, the request handler rejects the call with `403 Missing scope: mcp`. Otherwise the request handler writes the scopes of the request into the `ActionContext`.

steps.title: Tool list
steps.text: For `tools/list`, the tool provider lists an action only if the scopes of the request contain every scope of the action. The tool provider leaves out every action with the scope `mcp`, also the action `mcp`.

steps.title: Tool call
steps.text: For `tools/call`, the MCP server checks the scopes again with the same filter. If a scope of the MCP tool is missing, the MCP server returns the JSON-RPC error `-32602` with the message `Unknown tool`, the same error as for a tool that does not exist.

steps.title: Nested invocation
steps.text: The MCP tool calls the action through the `ActionInvoker`, without a second HTTP request. The `ToolContext` copies the backend user, the request and the scopes of the call to `mcp`. The `ActionInvoker` does not check the scopes again.

scopes mcp, dashboard:read H->>R: request with the scopes alt scope mcp not granted R-->>A: 403 Missing scope: mcp end R->>M: ActionContext with the scopes M->>P: tool fetch_dashboards, scopes of the context alt scope dashboard:read not granted P-->>A: JSON-RPC error -32602 Unknown tool end P->>I: invoke dashboards with the ToolContext Note over I: Same backend user, same scopes
no second scope check I->>D: call the method for the user D-->>I: result I-->>M: validated result M-->>A: 200 structuredContent

mcp.note: The command `mcp:serve` runs the MCP server over stdio. The command calls the action `mcp` directly with all scopes that the backend user can hold. The request handler does not run, so the command does not check the scope `mcp`.
